m.h: This profit rate assumes sending 3 big game creatures into hiding within an hour. It also assumes both a fully upgraded hunter lodge and bait boxes. Without these, profit rates will decrease due to slower catch rates + banking.
m.post:
Due to variance in monster spawns, (1/16 chance for double encounters and 1/160 for triple), as well as anywhere from 5-7 instances occurring before sending a creature into hiding, this method may vary. Experienced players will likely be able to clear 3 monsters within slightly less than an hour.

When starting an instance, withdraw 6 of the necessary bait. Inventory should always be prioritised to handle a double encounter (8 logs, 6 vines), as these encounters increase gp/hr rates, but will prove much more difficult without anticipation. Likewise, it is highly recommended that in the beginning of an instance, you first make 18 spears. Then, if the hunter lodge is:

  • Fully upgraded: randomly pick one of the available frog types and make 3 poison spears of the same colour and proceed to gather logs and vines to make the traps. This will provide a 50/50 chance of killing the creature on the first try. If the wrong colour was chosen, fix the traps that broke, and tip a few more spears--enough to deplete the creature's hp to zero.
  • Not fully upgraded: randomly choose two of the three colours, making two spears of one and one spear of the other coloured poison. These spears can deal either 7,500, 15,000 or 30,000 damage each. From the information gathered, finish the creature with any remaining required spears. This method guarantees no more than two spears will be required.

Skin the creature, deposit your loot in the bank box, and start again. Now that you know the 'correct' colour, on the second instance, prioritise tipping the rest of your spears before gathering more logs/vines, as the frogs take a few minutes to regain their colour.

For most Big Game Hunter creatures, dive is exceptionally useful in going from trap to trap, and surge is great for evading a monster's colour-zone. One may find it useful to put dive, surge, freedom, and anticipation keybound on an action bar, as they will all likely be needed for best results - especially in a triple encounter.

m.t: Turning extra fine sand into blessed sand
m.pg: Money making guide/Blessing extra fine sand
m.h:
Blessed sand is extra fine sand that has been blessed by using it on any altar of Saradomin. It is part of the process of making blessed molten glass. It can be blessed by using the "bless" option while standing next to an altar, or by using it on the altar directly. The most convenient place to make blessed sand seems to be at the Lumbridge Church.

The processing time is 2 ticks or 1.2 seconds per sand. This means in an hour (3,600 seconds) you can theoretically process 3,000 sand. The actual amount is closer to 2,800 depending on how AFK you are. Up to 60 blessed sand is made at a time. Knowing it takes 1.2 seconds per sand, you are able to AFK for 72 seconds between actions.

Extra fine sand can be blessed at more Saradomin-aligned altars, including:

  • Edgeville Monastery
  • Lumbridge Church
  • Entrana
  • Abbey of St. Elspeth Citharede
  • Everlight statues
  • Saradominist player-owned house chapels

m.pg: Money making guide/Brewing greenman's ale
m.h:
Inventory: Ectophial, Bucket of water, Bucket of water, Barley malt, Barley malt, The Stuff, Clean harralander, Clean harralander, Clean harralander, Clean harralander, Ale yeast, Calquat keg, Calquat keg

There are two locations to brew ales at: upstairs of the Laughing Miner Pub in Eastern Keldagrim and the basement of The Green Ghost inn in Port Phasmatys. Start with the vat in Keldagrim.

Fill your inventory with 2 empty buckets or buckets of water, 2 barley malts, 1 package of "The stuff", 4 clean harralander, two empty pots or pots of ale yeast (there is a pot respawn in Keldagrim), and 2 Calquat kegs. Head to the vat in Eastern Keldagrim via the trapdoor northwest of the Grand Exchange for the quickest access. The Laughing Miner Pub is located north of the mine carts, and northwest of the pub is a well to fill your empty buckets with water if they aren't already filled. Head to the pub and go upstairs to the brewery. Pick up two pots from the pot respawn near the vat if you don't have them already. Talk to Blandebir to fill up your two empty pots with ale yeast for 25 coins each. After you have all the necessary items, fill up the vat by putting in the two buckets of water, two barley malts, The Stuff, four clean harralanders and one pot of ale yeast. You must fill the vat in the correct order - don't forget The Stuff, it increases the chance of mature ale, which is worth more, to 50%. After you put the ale yeast in, the ale will begin to ferment. The vat in Keldagrim can take 8 hours to 2 days to finish fermenting.

Head back to the Grand Exchange via the mine carts, and withdraw the same items once again to fill the vat in Port Phasmatys. Withdraw an Ectophial for the quickest access to the brewery, 2 barley malts, 1 package of "The stuff", 4 clean harralander, and 2 Calquat kegs. You should have 2 empty buckets and 1 pot of ale yeast in your inventory from your earlier trip to Keldagrim. Use your Ectophial and head to The Green Ghost inn, southeast of the Ectofuntus. Go downstairs to the brewery, and use the tap on the far wall to fill up your empty buckets with water. Repeat the vat-filling process by putting in the two buckets of water, two barley malts, The Stuff, four clean harralanders and the last pot of ale yeast, in that order. After you put the ale yeast in, the ale will begin to ferment. The vat in Port Phasmatys takes a minimum of 2 days to ferment, but rarely exceeds that.

When a vat of greenman's ale is done, the examine text will say "This vat is filled with [mature] Greenman's ale." Click the valve on the vat to empty the vat into the nearby barrel, then use your Calquat keg on the barrel to collect the ale. If you check the Port Phasmatys ale two days after it begins fermenting to see if it's done, you can go through the same vat-filling process to collect and refill the ale vats, starting with Keldagrim, in one go.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying bagged plants
m.h:
The garden supplier sells bagged plants 1, which are the tertiary summoning ingredient for stranger plants.

  1. Starting at the east Falador bank (from either a Falador Teleport or the lodestone)
  2. Run to the garden supplier in Falador Park
  3. Buy 28 of the bagged plants 1
  4. Run back to the bank
  5. Repeat this 35 times

Keep in mind that because the plants are heavy, you will not be able to run for all 35 trips. It's worth visiting either the salt-water spring at Oo'glog (after completing As a First Resort) or the Anachronia Spa (after unlocking Tier 1 Spa) to take advantage of the unlimited energy buff.

Buying all 1000 plants should take about 25 minutes, but could take less if a Beast of Burden is utilised. It would take 25 trips with a spirit terrorbird, 22 with a war tortoise, and 18 with a pack yak assuming only 28 spaces are used to save time. After all plants have been bought, sell them at the Grand Exchange. They are not the most commonly traded item, so it may take a long time to sell them.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying balls of wool
m.h:
Ball of wool is used to train Crafting. There are many shops where one can buy balls of wool, however buying them from Jofridr Mordstatter is the quickest because of her proximity to a bank. Purchasing all the wool takes less than a minute. There are multiple ways of getting to Neitiznot

  1. Teleport to Rellekka via the Fremennik Province lodestone
  2. Run north west into town and take the boat to Neitiznot (north-east pier)
  3. Buy the balls of wool from Jofridr and bank them until she is out of stock
  4. When finished, sell them on the Grand Exchange

This method can be repeated in the other shop locations around Runescape, but the distance between the shop and bank is further away than on Neitiznot.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying broad arrowheads

rq.h: or Slayer cape, Ring of slaying, TokKul-Zo, or Ferocious ring
Being skulled If going to Noterazzo in the Bandit Camp.

m.h:
Broad arrowheads are often used in Fletching, and are one of the most commonly traded items in the game. Slayer shops sell 21000 of them a day for 50 coins each, and while the stock is shared between most of the shops, Turael and Spria in Burthorpe have an entirely separate stock, so up to 63000 total can be bought per day, from Turael/Spria and one other slayer master. Additionally, Notterazzo in the Wilderness Bandit Camp sells an additional 21000 daily, though this requires being skulled and has the risk of being killed.

The fastest way is to use the Slayer cape perk to quickly teleport to both Slayer masters. If the player doesn't own the cape, teleporting to Burthorpe via the Lodestone Network, then walking north and west to Turael/Spria is a good alternative. After buying the stock there, teleport to Sumona using a ring of slaying, and buy the stock there, then teleport to Edgeville and ask Vala to opt into PVP before running to the Wilderness camp. They can then be banked or sold on the Grand Exchange. Other slayer masters will also work, such as Kuradal (using the ferocious ring or the constructed fairy ring), Mazchna (using the Canifis lodestone), and Duradel/Lapalok (using the karamja gloves 3 teleport). Use the Wilderness sword 4's Edgeville teleport to leave the Wilderness quickly after buying Notterazzo's stock.

Note that the listed activity time is 2 minutes, but it could be much less if part of a larger daily run.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying buckets of milk
m.h:
Buy buckets of milk in The Milk Shop, from the milk seller in Falador farm, for 12 coins each. Bank with War's Retreat Teleport, then use the explorer's ring 3 to return.

There are 200 in stock, but this is a non-personalised shop; each world has a separate stock, so you can keep buying them indefinitely with enough worlds to cycle from and no competition. It takes 7 runs to get 196 buckets of milk in a world before hopping. Each world takes about 3 minutes and 45 seconds (225 seconds). That is 16 worlds per hour, or 3136 buckets of milk per hour.

The Milk Shop takes 100 minutes to fully restock, so you need about 27 worlds to do this continuously.

This can be done with no teleports, but would be much slower. Each world would take about 6 minutes (depositing milk at the bank deposit box in Port Sarim), for a theoretical 268*1960 - 23520 gp per hour, but in practice it would be less as it takes far more running and your energy would eventually deplete.

War's Retreat Teleport for banking can be substituted for the slower but practically requirements-free Archaeology journal. Either should only be used if the explorer ring 3 is available, as there are no other practical teleports to the Falador farm.

Theoretically magic notepaper can be used to note buckets of milk on the spot so banking is unnecessary (268 - 529 - 12 gp profit per bucket of milk), but there are only 32 free-to-play worlds, insufficient to sustain such an extreme rate of stock consumption (~100 worlds are needed). While stock lasts, a world can be cleared in 1 minute, theoretically amounting to an effective profit of 268*12000 - 529*12000 - 144000 gp per hour.

m.h:
The Bandit Duty Free shop, located in the Bandit Camp in level 23 Wilderness, sells various construction supplies at much lower than the GE guide price.

  • Before going to the Bandit Camp, PVP must be enabled to avoid the Bandit Camp NPCs from attacking you. Teleport to the Edgeville lodestone and speak to Vala to opt into PVP.
  • Next, bank all items except a method to teleport away while in level 23 wilderness if you have it, such as dragonstone teleport jewellery or Wilderness sword 4.
  • Teleport to the Wilderness Crater lodestone and run northwest until you reach the Bandit Camp.

    • If you enabled PVP in Edgeville, don't forget to return to Vala to opt out again if desired.

The margin of profit for this method may be much lower than the GE guide price might suggest. Construction materials such as the marble block and gold leaf may not sell at a profitable margin (or at all!). The large amount of starting cash required for this method, combined with the potential lack of resale value, makes this method risky and generally unprofitable.

Since some profit margins are super thin, it's recommend to check the profit margin for individual items before purchasing.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying crossbows from shops
m.h:
Crossbows are sometimes used for low level ranging training, but more commonly they are disassembled for components. You can buy more items from each of the shops but due to the small profit margins I have ignored them. The Crossbow Shop (Dwarven Mine) and Crossbow Shop (White Wolf Mountain) share the same stock, with White Wolf Mountain being slightly easier to get to.

A beast of burden will be useful if you have the summoning level for it. Start off by banking all items except, magic notepaper and equip a ring of wealth to travel to Keldagrim

  2. Run west and talk to Holoy at the Crossbow Shop (White Wolf Mountain)
  3. Buy all of the crossbows and note them
  4. Using your ring of wealth, teleport to Keldagrim
  5. Run around to the other side of the Consortium and talk to Hirko at the Crossbow Shop (Keldagrim)
  6. Buy all of the crossbows and note them
  7. Sell on the GE

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying feathers of Ma'at
m.h:
Feathers of Ma'at are required to kill Slayer monsters in the Sophanem Slayer Dungeon. Every day, 1000 feathers can be bought for 1500 coins each from the Menaphite guard outside the dungeon.

The fastest way to reach the guard is by using a Sophanem Slayer Dungeon teleport which teleports the player outside the dungeon and immediately next to the guard. If the player wishes to not use a teleportation tablet, the guard can be reached by teleporting to the lodestone in Menaphos and crossing the bridge to Sophanem. This requires completion of Jack of Spades and Contact! Players who own a mask of dust or a Helm of Devilry could also use this to teleport to the dungeon, if they have level 97 Slayer.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying from the Culinaromancer's Chest

rq.h: Partial or full completion of Recipe for Disaster

m.h:
The Culinaromancer's Chest sells various food-related items. The exact stock depends on how many of the Recipe for Disaster subquests have been completed, but when the entire quest has been completed, the listed stock will be available. The chest also acts as a bank, so buying and banking the items is relatively quick.

  1. Go to Lumbridge using the lodestone or the Lumbridge Teleport
  2. Head to the basement and start buying the listed items, closing the shop and banking each time

There are other profitable items, but the ones listed are the most efficient. Buying a few of each item for the first backpack full will allow more respawns to be bought, increasing the profit slightly. After stocking up on the food items, selling them on the Grand Exchange should be easy.

It's possible to increase profits further by grinding the chocolate bars into chocolate dust resulting in (1574 - 750) gp extra per bar.

There are other profitable items. Buying a few of each item for the first backpack full will allow more respawns to be bought, increasing the profit slightly. After stocking up on the culinary items, selling them on the Grand Exchange should be easy..

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying harpoons from Gerrant
m.h:
Gerrant's Fishy Business has a stock of 1,000 harpoons that he sells for 45 coins each. The stock replenishes fully every 24 hours. Since harpoons are worth 1,898 gp due to them being an ingredient in ibis pouches, buying all of the harpoons from Gerrant's shop and banking at the deposit box next to the Monks of Entrana is a good way to make money in free-to-play daily.

To get to the shop, use the Port Sarim lodestone, which takes you just a few feet away from the building. Go inside and buy 28 harpoons, and then run north-east to the deposit box on the docks. Run back to the shop and repeat. If you are running low on run energy, you could use the lodestone network to teleport from the deposit box to the shop, which takes about the same amount of time as running. If teleporting, make sure to utilise the "previous destination" right-click option on the lodestones. Each run takes about 40-45 seconds, so buying all 1000 harpoons takes about 25 minutes. When finished, re-sell the harpoons on the Grand Exchange.

Players with a Ring of Kinship may also teleport to Daemonheim to bank their harpoons.

Members can also use Harry's Fishing Shop in Catherby for the same purpose, and since it is closer to a bank, buying all 1000 harpoons will only take about 18-20 minutes. However only 300 will restock in 24h and members usually have much better ways to make money (even through other shop arbitrage) so this is not recommended.

m.t: Buying supplies from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found
m.pg: Money making guide/Buying items from Martin Thwait
m.h:
Martin Thwait's Lost and Found is a shop run by Martin Thwait in Rogue's Den. Buying some of the items he sells (lockpick along with most claws, knives and possibly rope) and banking them with Emerald Benedict, who usually wanders around the south-west corner of the Den, can be profitable.

The bronze, iron and black claws, along with the bronze and iron knives, can be harder to re-sell, so they weren't included in the inputs, outputs and profits. It is, of course, not necessary to buy all of the items listed here -- perhaps you just want to buy only the knives (since they stack and require no banking) with the adamant claws, depending on the current prices.

The fastest way to get there is to teleport to house, if the player-owned house located in Taverley, or simply access the Taverley lodestone using the Home Teleport and head east right away. Sell the items on the Grand Exchange when finished.

m.t: Buying items from both axe shops
m.pg: Money making guide/Buying items from axe shops
m.h:
This money making method is quite simple, the aim is to buy every item from both Axe shops and sell the items onto the GE.

  1. Start at Lumbridge lodestone with only magic notepaper in inventory
  2. Run south to Bob's Brilliant Axes
  3. Buy all of the items
  4. Bank everything apart from magic notepaper
  5. Teleport to Port Sarim lodestone
  6. Run north to Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar
  7. Buy all of the items

Using magic notepaper will greatly increase purchasing speed but costing 104,742 gp to note all items. Alternatively, using a beast of Burden will help speed up purchasing.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying items from farm shops
m.h:
Buying the stackable items means the daily moneymaker can be completed much quicker, there are however more items from the farm shops that return a profit; - compost, requiring to be banked or noted increasing the daily drastically.

  1. Teleport to Canifis lodestone
  2. Run East to Alice's farm shop and buy the item packs
  3. Teleport to Taverley lodestone
  4. Run north to Jones's farming shop and buy the item packs
  5. Teleport to Ardougne lodestone
  6. Run north to Richard's farming shop and buy the item packs
  7. Teleport to Port Sarim lodestone
  8. Run north to Sarah's farming shop and buy the item packs
  9. Teleport to Catherby lodestone
  10. Run west to Vanessa's farming shop and buy the item packs
m.post:
The above items respawn gradually over 1 week. They can be bought at any time with the reduced stock.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying items from pet shop
m.h:
The items from pet shops are used as food for animals within the player-owned farm, with other players often paying above mid price on the GE due to the low volume. The stock is shared between the two stores so it's only worth visiting one per day.

  1. Start by teleporting to the Taverley lodestone.
  2. Run south across the bridge and go into the pet shop.
  3. Buy all of the nuts, flies, and beetle bits.
  4. Sell everything on the Grand Exchange.

or

  1. Teleport to the Yanille lodestone.
  2. Run east to the pet shop.
  3. Buy all of the nuts, flies, and beetle bits.
  4. Sell everything on the Grand Exchange.

m.t: Buying kebabs from Karim in Al Kharid (Bank running)
m.pg: Money making guide/Buying kebabs from Karim
m.h:
This guide assumes 36 trips per hour. This method is simple but very click intensive due to purchasing each kebab one-by-one via dialogue options.

  1. Teleport to Al Kharid lodestone with an empty backpack
  2. Run west to Karim ()
  3. Talk to Karim to purchase one kebab
  4. Repeat previous step until you have a full backpack
  5. Run south (Surge or Dive/Bladed Dive can be helpful) and bank
  6. Run back to Karim
  7. Repeat

m.t: Buying maces from Flynn's Mace Market
m.pg: Money making guide/Buying maces from Flynn
m.h:
Maces are in demand as they are often disassembled for Invention materials, due to this demand players will often pay the higher price of the GE rather than visiting the shop.

Start this method with only magic notepaper in your inventory

  1. Teleport to Falador lodestone
  2. Run south to Flynn's Mace Market
  3. Buy all items and sell on the ge

Using the magic notepaper will cost 47,610 gp, this can be saved by running to the bank just south of the shop, taking 4 trips to buy all of the maces.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying meat from Chargurr
m.h: Fresh Meat is a shop owned by Chargurr in Oo'glog. The shop is located just north of the bank in the centre of town. The shop is easily accessible from the Oo'glog lodestone or by teleporting to Chief Tess using the Master archaeologist's outfit. Buying the meat pack, with the archaeologist outfit teleport, makes it a very quick daily activity to complete.

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying mithril seeds
m.h: Every 24 hours you can buy 500 mithril seeds at the Legends' Guild Shop of Useful Items and resell them on the grand exchange for a small daily profit

m.h:
Pickaxes are in demand to being essential for training Mining as well as being disassembled for Invention components, due to this demand players will often pay the higher price of the GE rather than visiting the shop.

Start this method with only 15 magic notepaper in your inventory

  1. Teleport to Falador lodestone
  2. Run north east towards the Ice Mountain
  3. Climb down the ladder
  4. Run south and then north past the forge and general store to get to Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop
  5. Buy all items and sell on the ge

m.pg: Money making guide/Buying plant cures
m.h: Buy plant cure from Head Farmer Jones's Farming Shop in Taverley for 40 coins each. After buying a full inventory deposit them at the bank to the south or use the War's Retreat Teleport for quick bank access. Then use the explorer's ring 3 to teleport to Sarah's Farming Shop near Falador and buy more plant cure. Home teleport, bank and buy another lot of plant cures at Vanessa's Farming Shop in Catherby. There are 10 in stock in each shop but it only takes about ~60 seconds for them to fully restock. Each trip takes about 2 minutes to get 28 potions. We can make approximately 30 trips per hour, so that gives us 840 potions per hour.

m.h:
Many types of runes can be bought from various rune shops for considerably less than their Grand Exchange market value. Many of these shops hold a stock of 7,000 of the basic elemental runes, of which most notably water runes, fire runes, and soul runes yield a notable profit when sold in the Grand Exchange. Upon arriving at a shop, purchase all of the profitable runes (see Outputs above).
Shops restock runes over 1 week so runs can be done more than just once a week, but will have a reduced number available.

For information on profitability of shop-bought runes in comparison to the Grand Exchange prices as well as available runes and which shops sell which, see this calculator.

Changing the buy warning value in shop warning options in the gameplay setting to at least 793,800 will remove any warning when trying to buy 2,100 nature or law runes at once. This can help quicken the purchasing process.
